papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Effective and Responsible Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Benefits, Risks, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable deployment of large, high-performing deep models in resource-constrained settings by transferring knowledge from a cumbersome teacher to a compact student. KD delivers large gains in inference speed and memory while preserving much of the teacher's utility across NLP tasks (including question answering and sentence understanding) and other modalities. However, naive distillation can transfer undesirable properties such as bias, privacy leakage, or fragility to distribution shift and adversarial attacks. A combination of strategies—student-aware teacher design, multi-teacher curricula, selective sample distillation, data augmentation, adversarial and robust distillation, and privacy-aware ensembles—provides a pragmatic path to compress models while controlling fairness, robustness, and privacy trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression encompass methods that transfer information from larger, high-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, deployable models (students), or otherwise reduce network size while retaining performance. Approaches range from matching final predictions to aligning intermediate representations, and they address practical constraints such as limited data, privacy, device heterogeneity, and robustness. Recent work spans algorithmic mechanisms (soft targets, layer mapping, adversarial sample synthesis), application-specific pipelines (BERT compression, non-autoregressive translation, task-adaptive models), and theoretical interpretations that link distillation to regularization. This synthesis summarizes core techniques, practical extensions, and open challenges reported in recent literature.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Wide Neural Networks: Risk Bound, Data Efficiency and Imperfect Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a strategy of training a student network with guide of the soft output from a teacher network. It has been a successful method of model compression and knowledge transfer. However, currently knowledge distillation lacks a convincing theoretical understanding. On the other hand, recent finding on neural tangent kernel enables us to approximate a wide neural network with a linear model of the network's random features. In this paper, we theoretically analyze the knowledge distillation of a wide neural network. First we provide a transfer risk bound for the linearized model of the network. Then we propose a metric of the task's training difficulty, called data inefficiency. Based on this metric, we show that for a perfect teacher, a high ratio of teacher's soft labels can be beneficial. Finally, for the case of imperfect teacher, we find that hard labels can correct teacher's wrong prediction, which explains the practice of mixing hard and soft labels.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: The Practical Centrality of Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, versatile technique for shrinking large neural models while preserving much of their predictive power. Across NLP and broader deep learning applications, distillation enables faster inference, reduced memory footprint, and easier deployment in latency- and resource-constrained settings. When combined with teacher ensembles, online or self-distillation, task-adaptive search, and careful handling of soft labels and data augmentation, distillation can deliver near-teacher accuracy while addressing scalability, robustness, and domain transfer concerns. I argue that knowledge distillation should be a first-line approach for model compression in modern NLP pipelines, supplemented by principled choices about teachers, data, and optimization to realize its full benefits.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity models to smaller, deployable models. Across computer vision, speech, recommendation, and natural language tasks, KD has been used to reduce inference cost while retaining most of the teacher model's performance. Research has advanced along several complementary axes: (1) methods that shape what is transferred (logits, hidden representations, attention or task-specific signals), (2) how the transfer is performed (layer-wise, multi-teacher, adversarial or student-aware training), (3) strategies to cope with limited or no access to original training data, and (4) techniques that preserve privacy and improve training efficiency. These lines of work show that careful alignment of objectives, attention to capacity gaps between teacher and student, and tailoring distillation to task and data regimes are critical for effective compression. Remaining challenges include robust cross-domain transfer, principled selection of what to distill for a target task, and maintaining robustness and fairness in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile approach to compress large neural models into smaller, more deployable ones while preserving much of their performance. Contemporary work shows KD is not a single algorithm but a family of techniques that transfer knowledge via soft labels, intermediate feature supervision, layer-wise mappings, data augmentation, and even data-free synthesis. KD has been applied across modalities and tasks — from compressing large language and multimodal transformers to enabling lightweight generative models and resource-efficient inference on edge devices. Empirical and theoretical analyses have begun to explain when and why distillation works, how it transfers inductive biases, and which input-side interventions (e.g., mixup/CutMix variants) improve transfer. Practical challenges remain in aligning heterogeneous teacher–student architectures, operating under limited or private data, and deciding what form of teacher knowledge (logits, features, relations, or structural priors) best serves a given student architecture.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfer information from larger, often ensemble or higher-capacity teacher models to smaller student models to improve accuracy, robustness, interpretability, or resource efficiency. Over the past decade KD has been adapted beyond the original soft-label logits transfer: methods now target intermediate features, attention maps, channel-wise signals, and training curricula; they address deployment constraints such as low-precision arithmetic, absence of original data, heterogeneous device models, and federated settings. In NLP, distillation has been applied to compress pretrained language models, to enable multi-task or lifelong learning, and to improve robustness in tasks such as question answering and machine translation. Practical recipes combine architectural adjustments, selective or staged distillation, and application-specific modifications to retain teacher strengths while avoiding transferred errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression encompass a set of techniques to transfer knowledge from larger, more expensive models (teachers) into smaller, faster models (students). Approaches vary from soft-label supervision and internal representation matching to data-free synthesis, task-adaptive architecture search, and privacy- or communication-aware protocols. Empirical results across vision and language tasks show distilled students can approach teacher performance while enabling deployment under computational, storage, privacy, or bandwidth constraints; open challenges include robustness, heterogeneity of data and models, and few-shot or label-scarce regimes.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and pragmatic framework for compressing large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, or more private models across modalities and tasks. When applied thoughtfully — by matching outputs, intermediate representations, training dynamics, or ensembles — KD can preserve or even improve task performance while enabling low-latency inference, reduced memory/compute, and new deployment modes (e.g., federated, data-free, or low-precision). However, distillation is not automatic: design choices about what to transfer, when to transfer, and how to align teacher and student matter for robustness, domain shifts, and rare-token behavior. I argue that best practice combines representation-aware objectives, selective or collaborative teaching strategies, and deployment-aware constraints (privacy, communication, numeric precision) to realize the full benefits of distillation in NLP and other deep learning settings.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Best Practices and Evidence for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) enables deployment of high-performing but large neural models by training compact student models that mimic larger teachers. Empirical work across speech, NLP, vision, and federated settings shows KD reduces model size and inference cost while preserving accuracy, and its effectiveness increases when combined with complementary techniques: pre-training compact architectures, adaptive layer mapping for transformers, data-centric augmentations, ensemble teachers, and robustness-aware objectives. This paper synthesizes results from recent studies to argue that a principled KD pipeline—pre-train compact students, match representations flexibly, leverage data augmentation and teacher ensembles, and incorporate robustness or task-specific objectives—yields the best tradeoff between efficiency and performance for practical deployments.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Theory, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or complex models into smaller, faster, or more constrained students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from a teacher. Over the past decade this has produced a diverse set of recipes — from logits/soft-label supervision to feature and layer-wise matching, progressive module replacement, data-free or privacy-aware distillation, and distributed/online variants — that together address deployment, privacy, robustness, and resource heterogeneity. Empirical work demonstrates that distilled students can approach teacher performance in NLP and vision tasks while enabling faster inference, lower memory use, or operation on weak devices; theoretical and empirical analyses illuminate when soft labels help, when hard labels or sample selection are needed, and how augmentation or task-aware selection of teacher knowledge improves transfer. Remaining challenges include principled understanding of which teacher signals are most useful for a given target task and resource constraint, robust and private distillation without original data, and scalable distillation in large distributed training regimes.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Distilling Object Detectors with Fine-grained Feature Imitation
papers_seen.abstract: State-of-the-art CNN based recognition models are often computationally prohibitive to deploy on low-end devices. A promising high level approach tackling this limitation is knowledge distillation, which let small student model mimic cumbersome teacher model's output to get improved generalization. However, related methods mainly focus on simple task of classification while do not consider complex tasks like object detection. We show applying the vanilla knowledge distillation to detection model gets minor gain. To address the challenge of distilling knowledge in detection model, we propose a fine-grained feature imitation method exploiting the cross-location discrepancy of feature response. Our intuition is that detectors care more about local near object regions. Thus the discrepancy of feature response on the near object anchor locations reveals important information of how teacher model tends to generalize. We design a novel mechanism to estimate those locations and let student model imitate the teacher on them to get enhanced performance. We first validate the idea on a developed lightweight toy detector which carries simplest notion of current state-of-the-art anchor based detection models on challenging KITTI dataset, our method generates up to 15% boost of mAP for the student model compared to the non-imitated counterpart. We then extensively evaluate the method with Faster R-CNN model under various scenarios with common object detection benchmark of Pascal VOC and COCO, imitation alleviates up to 74% performance drop of student model compared to teacher. Codes released at https://github.com/twangnh/Distilling-Object-Detectors

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide effective ways to reduce the computational and memory costs of large deep models while retaining much of their performance. Approaches span soft-target (logit) distillation, feature- and layer-level matching, data-augmentation and data-free techniques, and multi-teacher or teacher-optimization strategies. Recent work emphasizes task-aware alignment between teacher and student representations, augmentation schemes that improve teacher-student consistency, and training teachers that are explicitly optimized to help downstream students, enabling more reliable deployment in low-resource and privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Learning Perception-Aware Agile Flight in Cluttered Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, neural control policies have outperformed existing model-based planning-and-control methods for autonomously navigating quadrotors through cluttered environments in minimum time. However, they are not perception aware, a crucial requirement in vision-based navigation due to the camera's limited field of view and the underactuated nature of a quadrotor. We propose a learning-based system that achieves perception-aware, agile flight in cluttered environments. Our method combines imitation learning with reinforcement learning (RL) by leveraging a privileged learning-by-cheating framework. Using RL, we first train a perception-aware teacher policy with full-state information to fly in minimum time through cluttered environments. Then, we use imitation learning to distill its knowledge into a vision-based student policy that only perceives the environment via a camera. Our approach tightly couples perception and control, showing a significant advantage in computation speed (10 times faster) and success rate. We demonstrate the closed-loop control performance using hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and widely applicable approach to compress large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their performance. Across modalities and tasks—language understanding, retrieval, visual recognition, graph-based prediction, and data-limited or privacy-constrained settings—distillation enables latency- and resource-constrained deployment. However, straightforward distillation is not a panacea: distribution shifts, heterogeneity of data and models, and absence of training data expose weaknesses that require complementary techniques (e.g., internal representation matching, layer mapping, task-aware selection, generative replay). Combining these advances yields compressed models that are both accurate and robust for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Across modalities and tasks, distillation can be combined with architectural replacement, layer mapping, and task-adaptive search to produce compact models that meet latency and capacity constraints. However, the benefits of distillation depend strongly on teacher quality, data complexity, and which examples or representations are used for transfer; naive application can propagate teacher errors or harm low-frequency predictions. Careful design—using task-aware compression, selective or mixed supervision, and targeted remedies for dataset artifacts—enables distillation to deliver efficient, robust models for real-world NLP and vision systems.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated framework that enables transferring predictive power from large, expensive models to smaller, deployable ones. KD supports diverse practical constraints — absent training data, limited downstream-task data, domain shifts, multi-task settings, and architectural mismatches — and couples naturally with automated model search and targeted feature imitation. By viewing KD as a family of techniques (logit transfer, feature mimicking, adversarial-sample guidance, synthetic-data distillation, and teacher-ensemble strategies) practitioners can compress models while retaining or even improving task-relevant inductive structure and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Compact, Robust, and Adaptable Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible framework for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers while enabling domain adaptation, deployment under resource constraints, privacy-preserving releases, and improved robustness. KD techniques span transfer from full teacher ensembles to single students, intermediate-layer alignment, self-distillation, and even data-free distillation; each variant addresses different operational constraints. However, distillation also carries risks (e.g., transfer of undesirable biases) and requires careful design choices (e.g., what information to transfer and what data to use). Combining advances across these variants yields effective, small NLP models fit for real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: The Practical Centrality and Limitations of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a pragmatic and flexible approach to compressing large neural models so they can be deployed under memory, latency, privacy, or domain constraints. KD enables substantial reductions in size and compute while retaining much of a teacher model's performance, and it adapts well to modalities from vision to speech and to task-specific constraints in NLP. At the same time, KD is not a panacea: optimization difficulties, mismatches between teacher and student, and the potential for poorer outcomes when distilling inappropriate teacher signals require careful method selection and evaluation. Best practice therefore combines tailored distillation architectures, curriculum or multi-teacher strategies, privacy-aware mechanisms where needed, and awareness of when label-smoothing or teacher-free alternatives are preferable.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Wide Neural Networks: Risk Bound, Data Efficiency and Imperfect Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a strategy of training a student network with guide of the soft output from a teacher network. It has been a successful method of model compression and knowledge transfer. However, currently knowledge distillation lacks a convincing theoretical understanding. On the other hand, recent finding on neural tangent kernel enables us to approximate a wide neural network with a linear model of the network's random features. In this paper, we theoretically analyze the knowledge distillation of a wide neural network. First we provide a transfer risk bound for the linearized model of the network. Then we propose a metric of the task's training difficulty, called data inefficiency. Based on this metric, we show that for a perfect teacher, a high ratio of teacher's soft labels can be beneficial. Finally, for the case of imperfect teacher, we find that hard labels can correct teacher's wrong prediction, which explains the practice of mixing hard and soft labels.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, insights, and practical trends
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in latency-, memory-, and compute-constrained settings. Work across speech, NLP, vision, and graph domains demonstrates a spectrum of approaches: matching teacher output distributions, aligning intermediate features, progressively replacing modules, augmenting or synthesizing training data for better student generalization, and compressing ensembles into single models. Empirical results show substantial speed and size gains with modest accuracy loss when methods are carefully matched to task and architecture. Important themes include (1) the role of dark/soft labels vs. intermediate feature signals, (2) architectural or task-aware compression (including search), (3) techniques that increase the student’s exposure to informative training points (e.g., mixup or adversarial examples), and (4) distillation strategies tailored for ensembles or heterogeneous teacher–student pairs. Open challenges remain in principled sample selection, robust transfer of inductive biases, and automated trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Theory, and Practical Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach to compress large deep models and transfer knowledge to smaller, faster, or more interpretable models. Across vision and language applications, KD encompasses teacher-student paradigms that use teacher soft targets, intermediate representations, or auxiliary objectives; extensions include multi-teacher setups, data-free distillation, meta-learned teachers, and device-aware distillation for heterogeneous deployments. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of the teacher performance while enabling orders-of-magnitude reductions in parameters and inference cost; theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when and why distillation helps and how dataset complexity, teacher quality, and student capacity interact to determine outcomes. Practical strategies combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware techniques to meet deployment constraints while retaining generalization.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: The Role and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their performance. KD is applicable across modalities and tasks, from machine translation and reading comprehension to distributed training and privacy-sensitive deployment. Success depends on aligning teacher and student representations, selecting appropriate knowledge (logits, intermediate features, attention, contrastive signals), and matching methods to constraints such as limited data, heterogeneous devices, or privacy requirements. Theoretical analyses and practical advances both show that careful design choices — including attention-based matching, layer projection, task-aware filtering, online collaboration, multi-teacher weighting, and privacy-aware perturbation — materially affect outcomes and trade-offs between fidelity, efficiency, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer information from larger or more informative models (teachers) into smaller or more efficient models (students). Research across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks has developed multiple KD objectives (soft-label matching, intermediate layer alignment, contrastive/representation losses), training regimes (offline teacher-student, online co-training, meta-learned teacher updates), and architecture-aware compression strategies (channel-wise attention, task-adaptive architecture search). Empirical and theoretical work highlights tradeoffs between bias and variance introduced by soft targets, the value of pre-training compact models before distillation, and the importance of data and augmentation choices for effective transfer. Emerging large-scale and privacy-aware deployments leverage online and federated distillation variants to reduce communication and improve reproducibility, while new approaches aim to make teachers more student-friendly or distill internal representations rather than only outputs. Key open challenges include matching representational structure across heterogeneous architectures, choosing what and when to distill, and scaling methods to very large datasets and distributed settings while preserving privacy and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Outcomes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity models into smaller, faster models by transferring information from a teacher to a student. Approaches vary from matching final soft targets to transferring intermediate representations, leveraging ensembles or multiple teachers, to data-free synthesis and combining KD with pruning or low-precision numerics. In NLP, KD has enabled compact models to approach the performance of large pre-trained models while substantially reducing inference cost. Recent work clarifies theoretical mechanisms, proposes many-to-many layer alignment techniques, and develops adaptive multi-teacher weighting and zero-shot distillation to broaden applicability. Despite strong empirical gains, open challenges remain in task-specific alignment, robustness to heterogeneous data, and preserving fairness and calibration during compression.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Attention-Guided Answer Distillation for Machine Reading Comprehension
papers_seen.abstract: Despite that current reading comprehension systems have achieved significant advancements, their promising performances are often obtained at the cost of making an ensemble of numerous models. Besides, existing approaches are also vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper tackles these problems by leveraging knowledge distillation, which aims to transfer knowledge from an ensemble model to a single model. We first demonstrate that vanilla knowledge distillation applied to answer span prediction is effective for reading comprehension systems. We then propose two novel approaches that not only penalize the prediction on confusing answers but also guide the training with alignment information distilled from the ensemble. Experiments show that our best student model has only a slight drop of 0.4% F1 on the SQuAD test set compared to the ensemble teacher, while running 12x faster during inference. It even outperforms the teacher on adversarial SQuAD datasets and NarrativeQA benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Path to Compact, High-Quality Models in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models for deployment. Across NLP and other modalities, distillation enables lightweight architectures to retain much of a teacher's performance while supporting additional compression techniques (pruning, quantization) and privacy-respecting or data-free workflows. However, distillation outcomes depend strongly on teacher–student compatibility, the form of distilled knowledge (logits, features, attention), access to data, and optimization choices. Best results arise when distillation is integrated with appropriate pre-training, architectural adapters (projectors or attention alignment), and, when necessary, data synthesis or domain adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring useful information from teacher models. Across vision, speech, reinforcement learning, and NLP, KD has been adapted into logit-level supervision, intermediate feature and layer-wise matching, data augmentation strategies, data-free setups, and training-time architectural replacement. Recent work has expanded KD to address practical constraints—privacy in federated settings, bias mitigation in language models, low-precision deployment, and multi-task transfer—while also proposing task-aware and capacity-aware methods to reduce redundant or harmful teacher signals. This synthesis summarizes the mechanisms, extensions, strengths, and limitations documented in contemporary studies and highlights promising directions for making distilled models both efficient and robust.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Learning Perception-Aware Agile Flight in Cluttered Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, neural control policies have outperformed existing model-based planning-and-control methods for autonomously navigating quadrotors through cluttered environments in minimum time. However, they are not perception aware, a crucial requirement in vision-based navigation due to the camera's limited field of view and the underactuated nature of a quadrotor. We propose a learning-based system that achieves perception-aware, agile flight in cluttered environments. Our method combines imitation learning with reinforcement learning (RL) by leveraging a privileged learning-by-cheating framework. Using RL, we first train a perception-aware teacher policy with full-state information to fly in minimum time through cluttered environments. Then, we use imitation learning to distill its knowledge into a vision-based student policy that only perceives the environment via a camera. Our approach tightly couples perception and control, showing a significant advantage in computation speed (10 times faster) and success rate. We demonstrate the closed-loop control performance using hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Multi-purpose Strategy for Model Compression and Robust Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving or even improving task performance. Beyond simple size reduction, KD supports domain adaptation, latency-aware architecture transformations, robustness transfer, and interpretable model surrogates. When combined with careful training protocols (e.g., multi-teacher schemes, domain adaptation, or targeted regularization), distillation enables deployment of high-performing models in resource- and latency-constrained or safety-critical settings across vision, speech, 3D perception, and natural language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Compact, Robust, and Adaptable Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible framework for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers while enabling domain adaptation, deployment under resource constraints, privacy-preserving releases, and improved robustness. KD techniques span transfer from full teacher ensembles to single students, intermediate-layer alignment, self-distillation, and even data-free distillation; each variant addresses different operational constraints. However, distillation also carries risks (e.g., transfer of undesirable biases) and requires careful design choices (e.g., what information to transfer and what data to use). Combining advances across these variants yields effective, small NLP models fit for real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable smaller or faster models to retain much of the performance of larger teachers by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or task-specific inductive biases. Work in this area spans supervised soft-target matching, intermediate-layer representation transfer, many-to-many layer alignment, data-free distillation, multi-teacher and ensemble-derived strategies, and online/distributed variants that exploit parallelism. Applications include compressing large pretrained language models for downstream NLP tasks, accelerating inference for computer vision and generative models, and producing interpretable or privacy-preserving compact models for healthcare and on-device deployment. Important trade-offs involve what form of knowledge is transferred (logits, activations, relations), access to training data, robustness to domain heterogeneity, and how to balance capacity, efficiency, and generalization in student models.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable smaller, faster models to inherit performance characteristics from larger models. Research has introduced multiple KD paradigms—teacher-student soft-label transfer, self-distillation, feature/internal-representation matching, multi-teacher strategies, and data-augmentation–aware distillation—each addressing different practical constraints such as domain shift, resource limits, or heterogeneous architectures. Applications span speech, machine translation evaluation, ASR, and domain-specific pretrained models; empirical work shows substantial reductions in model size and latency can be achieved with modest accuracy loss, or sometimes even gains, when distillation is combined with architectural adaptations and training-time strategies. Remaining challenges include transferring internal representations across heterogeneous architectures, choosing or designing teachers that are most useful for particular students, and preserving low-frequency or domain-specific signals during aggressive compression.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Effective Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression are indispensable tools to deploy high-performing deep models under compute, memory, privacy, and latency constraints. Across modalities and tasks, effective compression requires more than copying teacher logits: practitioners should match richer internal representations, align inputs and tokenization across teacher and student, design teacher updates that explicitly optimize transfer, and account for privacy and robustness needs. When applied thoughtfully, KD can produce compact models that retain much of the teacher’s utility and in some cases improve efficiency beyond the original models.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses or transfers knowledge from larger, more expensive models (teachers) into smaller, cheaper models (students) by using richer supervision than hard labels alone. The literature has developed multiple complementary strategies—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, architecturally guided replacement, multi-teacher schedules, data- and privacy-aware variants, and teacher-training schemes—to address deployment constraints, domain shift, and limited or private data. Empirical work shows these approaches can close much of the performance gap to full-size models across classification, language understanding, and retrieval tasks; theoretical and empirical analyses explain why distillation often improves generalization beyond mere compression. Remaining challenges include input distribution mismatch, low-frequency token fidelity in sequence tasks, and robust distillation without access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Practices and Open Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce model size and inference cost by transferring information from a high-capacity source (teacher) to a smaller target (student). Across vision, speech, and NLP, practitioners combine logit-based supervision, feature imitation, data augmentation, and architectural or precision changes to preserve performance while shrinking computation. Recent work emphasizes (1) the role of pre-training for compact models, (2) task- and modality-specific distillation recipes, (3) data-availability and privacy constraints that motivate data-free or augmentation-based approaches, and (4) designing teachers or training procedures that improve transfer. These trends point toward hybrid pipelines that integrate pre-training, augmentation, and teacher-student co-design to get robust, efficient models for real-world deployments.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Best Practices and Evidence for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) enables deployment of high-performing but large neural models by training compact student models that mimic larger teachers. Empirical work across speech, NLP, vision, and federated settings shows KD reduces model size and inference cost while preserving accuracy, and its effectiveness increases when combined with complementary techniques: pre-training compact architectures, adaptive layer mapping for transformers, data-centric augmentations, ensemble teachers, and robustness-aware objectives. This paper synthesizes results from recent studies to argue that a principled KD pipeline—pre-train compact students, match representations flexibly, leverage data augmentation and teacher ensembles, and incorporate robustness or task-specific objectives—yields the best tradeoff between efficiency and performance for practical deployments.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation: Practical, Theoretical, and Methodological Evidence for Efficient Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central and mature approach for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from richer teacher models to compact students. Across modalities and tasks—NLP, vision, graph learning, and retrieval—KD enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while retaining most of the teacher's performance. Beyond pure compression, KD variants address practical deployment concerns: multi-teacher and confidence-aware schemes improve robustness to imperfect teachers; progressive and module-level replacement approaches enable deeper integrated compression; online/distillation-in-parallel techniques scale training and improve reproducibility; and targeted feature-distillation methods refine representational quality. Theory of wide networks provides guidance on when soft labels help and when mixing hard labels is beneficial. Together, empirical and theoretical work shows KD is a versatile, well-grounded toolbox for model compression and knowledge transfer in modern deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: The Strengths and Limitations of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large models into deployable, efficient students across modalities. Empirical work shows KD can preserve task performance while drastically reducing size and compute, but its success depends on choices of what and how to transfer, availability and provenance of data, and training dynamics. Advances in feature-matching, progressive module replacement, task-aware layer selection, data-free synthesis, and robustness-aware distillation expand KD's applicability but do not eliminate core challenges—optimization barriers, distribution heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and potential transfer of unwanted behaviors. A careful, task-aware combination of techniques is therefore required to realize reliable, compact models for production use.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Beyond Dark Knowledge: A Practical Position on How and Why Knowledge Distillation Works for Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile toolkit for compressing large models and adapting knowledge across architectures, domains, and devices. Its effectiveness derives from multiple mechanisms: soft-target regularization that shapes student generalization, representation-level transfer that preserves structure beyond logits, and methods that remove dependence on the teacher's training data. However, KD is not a single monolithic recipe — optimization dynamics, teacher-student mismatch, and interactions with other regularizers (e.g., label smoothing or fairness constraints) materially affect outcomes. I argue that practitioners should treat KD as a collection of complementary approaches (logit regularization, feature mimicking, contrastive alignment, data- or generator-based sample synthesis, and adaptive teacher selection) and choose combinations appropriate to their constraints (data availability, privacy, compute, heterogeneity). This perspective explains why simpler or even teacher-free approaches can match standard KD in many settings, and why representation- and adaptation-oriented variants expand KD’s applicability to domain adaptation, federated and graph models.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques have become central to deploying deep models under resource constraints. Methods extend beyond simple logit matching to include intermediate-layer supervision, feature mimicking, projector-based transforms, teacher-student co-training, and data- or domain-aware schemes. Distillation has been applied across modalities (vision, language, multimodal, graphs) and in settings with limited or no access to original training data. Practical advances address transfer across architectures, task-adaptive compression, and efficient architecture search, while open problems remain around distribution shift, heterogeneity of data or detectors, and preserving rare or low-frequency information.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a General-Purpose Compression Strategy for Deep Models: Evidence, Mechanisms, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a specialized technique for transferring softened output distributions into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing and adapting deep models across domains (vision, language, multimodal, and generative models). Empirical results across tasks show that KD can preserve or even improve accuracy while substantially reducing model size and latency, and it can be combined with complementary strategies (pre-training, low-precision arithmetic, data synthesis, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints and privacy requirements. However, effective distillation requires attention to what is transferred (logits, internal representations, attention maps), how teachers and students are aligned (layer mapping, input alignment), and whether real data are available (data-free or adversarially guided generation). This paper synthesizes evidence from recent work to argue that KD, when applied with these considerations, is a reliable foundation for practical model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible strategy for compressing large models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment in constrained environments. Advances across task-adaptive compression, data-free and zero-shot distillation, multi-teacher and meta-learned teaching, and self-distillation demonstrate KD's broad applicability. However, KD is not a panacea: success depends on data availability, the teacher–student optimization dynamics, and explicit design choices around architecture and training signals. Combining pre-training of compact models, task-aware architecture search, and sophisticated distillation protocols yields the best trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, and privacy.
