papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Work
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques enable deployment of large neural models by transferring knowledge from larger or multi-modal teachers to smaller or specialized students. Work in this area spans methods for structural student design, feature- and logit-level supervision, data-free or few-shot settings, low-precision inference, multi-teacher and domain-adaptive strategies, and automated discovery of compact architectures. Empirical results across vision, speech, language, graph, and generative models show that distillation often achieves substantial reductions in memory, compute, and latency while preserving much of the teacher performance; however, success depends on data availability, teacher–student mismatch, and training protocols. Remaining challenges include robust distillation under data heterogeneity, efficient training when teacher cost is high, and principled methods for combining multiple or heterogeneous teachers.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become primary tools to shrink large deep models for deployment while retaining much of their predictive power. Across vision, speech and natural language processing, researchers have developed a range of approaches that operate at the level of logits (soft labels), intermediate representations, modules/layers, or training curricula, and have combined KD with complementary strategies such as architecture search, quantization, and generative replay. Empirical work shows that distilled students can often approach teacher performance while achieving large reductions in size and latency, but the effectiveness of different KD strategies depends strongly on task, data distribution, teacher strength, and practical constraints such as availability of original training data. Important challenges remain in transferring robustness, handling heterogeneous or private data, preserving rare-token behavior, and balancing bias–variance tradeoffs introduced by soft supervision.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Path to Compressing and Deploying Deep Models in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible technique that enables transferring predictive power from large models into smaller or more efficient ones. When combined with complementary strategies such as pre-training of compact architectures, task-aware selection of distilled signals, quantization-aware training, and privacy-preserving or federated protocols, KD can make state-of-the-art models practically usable on resource-constrained and heterogeneous devices. However, realizing these gains requires attention to what is distilled (outputs versus internal representations), how distilled signals are selected for the target task, and whether data-privacy or communication constraints demand synthetic or distributed distillation procedures.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans algorithmic advances in teacher–student objectives, architecture-aware compression, data- and privacy-constrained distillation, and theoretical analyses that clarify when and why distillation helps. Practical work shows gains from combining KD with data augmentation, many-to-many layer mappings, and architecture search, while complementary efforts address data-free and privacy-preserving distillation. Remaining challenges include imperfect teachers, data heterogeneity, and adapting compression to task-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Approaches to Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques produce smaller, faster models by transferring knowledge from larger or ensemble teachers to compact students. Across modalities and tasks, researchers have developed diverse strategies—teacher–student logits matching, layer-wise representation matching, adversarial sample generation, progressive module replacement, many-to-many layer mapping, and task-aware filtering—to address capacity gaps, data access limits, privacy constraints, and robustness needs. Practical deployments additionally combine distillation with pruning, structured sparsity, and federated protocols to meet hardware and communication budgets. Empirical work shows that careful design of distillation objectives and inputs can preserve most of the teacher’s accuracy and even transfer properties such as adversarial robustness, while specialized schemes enable distillation without original training data or across continual/heterogeneous settings.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Effective Knowledge Distillation for Deployable Deep Models: Evidence, Techniques, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central tool to compress large deep models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. Across NLP and broader deep learning applications, KD has enabled domain adaptation, model-size reduction, cross-lingual transfer, and deployment under resource constraints. Success depends on (1) aligning teacher and student inputs and intermediate representations, (2) choosing appropriate supervision signals (soft labels, intermediate-feature losses, attention-based guidance), (3) handling the absence of original training data when necessary, and (4) adapting compression to task and domain requirements. This review synthesizes empirical and methodological findings from recent studies to recommend principled KD choices for practitioners aiming to deploy compact, robust models in real-world NLP and related tasks.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Multi-purpose Strategy for Model Compression and Robust Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving or even improving task performance. Beyond simple size reduction, KD supports domain adaptation, latency-aware architecture transformations, robustness transfer, and interpretable model surrogates. When combined with careful training protocols (e.g., multi-teacher schemes, domain adaptation, or targeted regularization), distillation enables deployment of high-performing models in resource- and latency-constrained or safety-critical settings across vision, speech, 3D perception, and natural language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a unifying, practical framework to compress large deep models into smaller, deployable students while addressing concerns of computation, privacy, robustness, and limited task data. KD techniques span from logits- and feature-based matching to progressive module replacement, multi-teacher ensembles, data-free (zero-shot) synthesis, and federated output-sharing, and when combined with careful data augmentation and generative replay they yield compact models that retain much of the teacher utility in real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: The Versatility and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and widely applicable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students while preserving much of their performance. Across domains — including reinforcement learning, vision, generative modeling, and language — distillation can accelerate inference, enable deployment on constrained devices, and transfer capabilities such as domain adaptation or lifelong learning. However, its effectiveness depends on choices about teacher-student pairing, data availability and augmentation, sample selection, and training protocols; it also interacts with privacy and heterogeneity constraints. A balanced approach that combines principled distillation objectives, appropriate data strategies (including data-free methods when necessary), and curriculum or annealing schedules yields the best tradeoffs between compactness and retained performance.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression approaches seek to transfer useful information from larger, often over-parameterized teacher models into smaller, deployable student models while preserving performance. Research has expanded beyond matching final logits to include feature- and layer-level supervision, adaptive layer alignments, many-to-many mappings, task-aware filtering, teacher-free alternatives, data- and communication-constrained settings, and careful use of input-side techniques such as data augmentation. Empirical work shows these strategies can yield compact models that approach teacher accuracy across vision and language tasks, and practical pipelines combine pre-training of compact architectures with targeted distillation to improve downstream performance and deployment efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation: Task-adaptive, Privacy-aware, and Feature-centric Compression for Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are now essential tools to deploy large deep models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. When applied thoughtfully—adapting to task requirements, leveraging feature-level signals, and accounting for data availability—KD can yield compact models that retain much of the teacher's performance while improving inference speed, memory footprint, and interpretability. However, naive distillation can fail under data heterogeneity, limited data, or strong teacher–student mismatches; addressing these requires task-aware layer selection, multi-teacher strategies, and alternatives to standard logit matching. I argue that the most effective KD pipelines combine task-adaptive compression, feature-directed supervision, and methods that preserve privacy and robustness to limited data.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide effective ways to reduce the computational and memory costs of large deep models while retaining much of their performance. Approaches span soft-target (logit) distillation, feature- and layer-level matching, data-augmentation and data-free techniques, and multi-teacher or teacher-optimization strategies. Recent work emphasizes task-aware alignment between teacher and student representations, augmentation schemes that improve teacher-student consistency, and training teachers that are explicitly optimized to help downstream students, enabling more reliable deployment in low-resource and privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Learning Student Networks via Feature Embedding
papers_seen.abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have been widely used in numerous applications, but their demanding storage and computational resource requirements prevent their applications on mobile devices. Knowledge distillation aims to optimize a portable student network by taking the knowledge from a well-trained heavy teacher network. Traditional teacher-student based methods used to rely on additional fully-connected layers to bridge intermediate layers of teacher and student networks, which brings in a large number of auxiliary parameters. In contrast, this paper aims to propagate information from teacher to student without introducing new variables which need to be optimized. We regard the teacher-student paradigm from a new perspective of feature embedding. By introducing the locality preserving loss, the student network is encouraged to generate the low-dimensional features which could inherit intrinsic properties of their corresponding high-dimensional features from teacher network. The resulting portable network thus can naturally maintain the performance as that of the teacher network. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify the lower computation complexity of the proposed method. Experiments on benchmark datasets and well-trained networks suggest that the proposed algorithm is superior to state-of-the-art teacher-student learning methods in terms of computational and storage complexity.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Motivations, and Open Questions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression encompass a set of techniques that transfer information from larger or more complex models (teachers) to smaller or more efficient models (students). These practices are used both to reduce inference cost and to adapt large models to constrained or specialized settings (privacy-preserving deployment, edge devices, or faster generation). Across applications—classification, sequence modeling, graph learning, speech, and machine translation—research has explored what to transfer (logits, features, representations), how to transfer it (soft labels, feature projectors, adversarial objectives, data augmentation), and when transfer can fail or require modification (noisy labels, distributional shifts, imperfect teachers). Empirical and theoretical work shows benefits but also identifies trade-offs (regularization vs. fidelity, robustness transfer limits, and data requirements), motivating hybrid approaches that combine pre-training, careful sample selection, and augmentation.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Methods and Challenges in Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger, more expensive teacher models to smaller, faster student models. Across vision, generative modeling, and NLP, researchers have developed logit- and feature-level distillation, task-specific adaptations, multi-teacher schemes, and teacher-optimization strategies to improve student accuracy, robustness, and efficiency. Work also focuses on constraints arising in distributed and privacy-preserving settings, on preserving rare or fine-grained information, and on adapting distillation to complex tasks such as detection, generation, and dense prediction. Practical systems combine architectural choices, training curricula, and distilled supervision to achieve favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs for deployment.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Best Practices and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Efficient Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a foundational technique for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the accuracy of larger teachers across vision, language, speech, and graph domains. When applied thoughtfully — combining representational objectives, teacher-student co-design, task-aware compression, and appropriate data strategies — KD enables deployment on resource-constrained devices while maintaining robustness and fairness. However, pitfalls arise from mismatches in inputs, teacher strength, data availability, and dataset biases; practical KD should therefore be integrated with complementary methods (e.g., architecture search, pruning, curriculum strategies, and data-generation) and with safeguards for ethical concerns.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic training trick into a unifying framework for producing compact, efficient models across vision, speech, and language tasks. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble consensus from larger teachers to smaller students, KD enables substantial reductions in memory, compute, and latency while largely preserving accuracy. Beyond plain size reduction, KD adapts to constraints that arise in real deployments — limited data or privacy-sensitive settings, heterogeneous architectures, and modality gaps — through techniques such as feature-level alignment, selective sampling, ensemble-to-single-model transfer, and data-free synthesis. As a practical bridge between research-scale architectures and deployable systems, KD complements other compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and serves both as an efficiency accelerator and as a lever for robustness and domain generalization.

Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively."}, {'author': 'Daniel', 'year': 2020, 'title': 'Data-Free Adversarial Distillation', 'abstract': 'Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer information from larger or more informative models (teachers) into smaller or more efficient models (students). Research across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks has developed multiple KD objectives (soft-label matching, intermediate layer alignment, contrastive/representation losses), training regimes (offline teacher-student, online co-training, meta-learned teacher updates), and architecture-aware compression strategies (channel-wise attention, task-adaptive architecture search). Empirical and theoretical work highlights tradeoffs between bias and variance introduced by soft targets, the value of pre-training compact models before distillation, and the importance of data and augmentation choices for effective transfer. Emerging large-scale and privacy-aware deployments leverage online and federated distillation variants to reduce communication and improve reproducibility, while new approaches aim to make teachers more student-friendly or distill internal representations rather than only outputs. Key open challenges include matching representational structure across heterogeneous architectures, choosing what and when to distill, and scaling methods to very large datasets and distributed settings while preserving privacy and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Learning Perception-Aware Agile Flight in Cluttered Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, neural control policies have outperformed existing model-based planning-and-control methods for autonomously navigating quadrotors through cluttered environments in minimum time. However, they are not perception aware, a crucial requirement in vision-based navigation due to the camera's limited field of view and the underactuated nature of a quadrotor. We propose a learning-based system that achieves perception-aware, agile flight in cluttered environments. Our method combines imitation learning with reinforcement learning (RL) by leveraging a privileged learning-by-cheating framework. Using RL, we first train a perception-aware teacher policy with full-state information to fly in minimum time through cluttered environments. Then, we use imitation learning to distill its knowledge into a vision-based student policy that only perceives the environment via a camera. Our approach tightly couples perception and control, showing a significant advantage in computation speed (10 times faster) and success rate. We demonstrate the closed-loop control performance using hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression encompass methods that transfer information from larger, high-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, deployable models (students), or otherwise reduce network size while retaining performance. Approaches range from matching final predictions to aligning intermediate representations, and they address practical constraints such as limited data, privacy, device heterogeneity, and robustness. Recent work spans algorithmic mechanisms (soft targets, layer mapping, adversarial sample synthesis), application-specific pipelines (BERT compression, non-autoregressive translation, task-adaptive models), and theoretical interpretations that link distillation to regularization. This synthesis summarizes core techniques, practical extensions, and open challenges reported in recent literature.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and compression seek to retain performance of large deep models while reducing size and latency for deployment. Methods extend beyond matching soft teacher outputs to include transferring internal representations, attention maps, and relational or adversarial signals; they can be applied during pretraining, task fine-tuning, or domain adaptation, and may operate with or without access to original training data. Empirical results across retrieval, reading comprehension, pretrained language models, and other domains show consistent trade-offs where careful choice of distillation targets, training curricula, and data augmentation materially improves student generalization and robustness while substantially lowering compute and memory requirements.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: The Practical Case for Knowledge Distillation in NLP: Effectiveness, Mechanisms, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques are a practical and necessary pathway to deploy high-performing pre-trained language models in resource-constrained settings. Distillation enables large teacher models to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations to smaller students, preserving much of the original performance while reducing inference cost. However, the success of distillation depends on choices across pre-training, teacher strength, layer- and feature-level alignment, data used for transfer, and augmentation or curriculum strategies. When these components are designed together, distilled models can approach teacher-level performance and enable real-world NLP systems at lower latency and cost.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller ones by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations from a teacher to a student. Over the past decade KD methods have diversified beyond simple logit matching to include intermediate-feature imitation, multi-teacher pipelines, data-free approaches, and task-adaptive compression. Empirical work across NLP, speech, vision-language, and other domains shows KD can preserve most of a teacher's performance while drastically reducing model size and latency. Theoretical and empirical analyses have clarified why KD works in many settings (regularization via soft targets, ensemble-induced dark knowledge, and representation enrichment), but open problems remain in data privacy, distribution shift, automated student design, and guarantees for out-of-distribution robustness.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Practical Case for Richer Knowledge Distillation in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a necessary and practical tool for compressing large models and enabling deployment in resource-constrained settings, but its value depends critically on what is distilled and how. Soft-label matching transfers useful "dark knowledge" from ensembles, yet by itself often fails to capture internal structure, handle domain or data heterogeneity, or operate when original data are unavailable. Combining soft labels with internal- and feature-level guidance, architecture- and task-aware compression, and data- or privacy-aware generation strategies yields more robust, compact models that retain teacher performance across NLP and broader deep learning tasks.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable smaller or faster models to retain much of the performance of larger teachers by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or task-specific inductive biases. Work in this area spans supervised soft-target matching, intermediate-layer representation transfer, many-to-many layer alignment, data-free distillation, multi-teacher and ensemble-derived strategies, and online/distributed variants that exploit parallelism. Applications include compressing large pretrained language models for downstream NLP tasks, accelerating inference for computer vision and generative models, and producing interpretable or privacy-preserving compact models for healthcare and on-device deployment. Important trade-offs involve what form of knowledge is transferred (logits, activations, relations), access to training data, robustness to domain heterogeneity, and how to balance capacity, efficiency, and generalization in student models.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Multi-purpose Strategy for Model Compression and Robust Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving or even improving task performance. Beyond simple size reduction, KD supports domain adaptation, latency-aware architecture transformations, robustness transfer, and interpretable model surrogates. When combined with careful training protocols (e.g., multi-teacher schemes, domain adaptation, or targeted regularization), distillation enables deployment of high-performing models in resource- and latency-constrained or safety-critical settings across vision, speech, 3D perception, and natural language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: DINE: Domain Adaptation from Single and Multiple Black-box Predictors
papers_seen.abstract: To ease the burden of labeling, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge in previous and related labeled datasets (sources) to a new unlabeled dataset (target). Despite impressive progress, prior methods always need to access the raw source data and develop data-dependent alignment approaches to recognize the target samples in a transductive learning manner, which may raise privacy concerns from source individuals. Several recent studies resort to an alternative solution by exploiting the well-trained white-box model from the source domain, yet, it may still leak the raw data through generative adversarial learning. This paper studies a practical and interesting setting for UDA, where only black-box source models (i.e., only network predictions are available) are provided during adaptation in the target domain. To solve this problem, we propose a new two-step knowledge adaptation framework called DIstill and fine-tuNE (DINE). Taking into consideration the target data structure, DINE first distills the knowledge from the source predictor to a customized target model, then fine-tunes the distilled model to further fit the target domain. Besides, neural networks are not required to be identical across domains in DINE, even allowing effective adaptation on a low-resource device. Empirical results on three UDA scenarios (i.e., single-source, multi-source, and partial-set) confirm that DINE achieves highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art data-dependent approaches. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/tim-learn/DINE/}.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Approaches to Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques produce smaller, faster models by transferring knowledge from larger or ensemble teachers to compact students. Across modalities and tasks, researchers have developed diverse strategies—teacher–student logits matching, layer-wise representation matching, adversarial sample generation, progressive module replacement, many-to-many layer mapping, and task-aware filtering—to address capacity gaps, data access limits, privacy constraints, and robustness needs. Practical deployments additionally combine distillation with pruning, structured sparsity, and federated protocols to meet hardware and communication budgets. Empirical work shows that careful design of distillation objectives and inputs can preserve most of the teacher’s accuracy and even transfer properties such as adversarial robustness, while specialized schemes enable distillation without original training data or across continual/heterogeneous settings.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a single compression trick but a flexible set of techniques that can reduce model size, preserve or transfer task-relevant information, enable deployment in latency- and memory-constrained settings, support domain adaptation and privacy-preserving federated workflows, and be combined with structural compression. When applied thoughtfully — with task-aware selection of distilled signals, architecturally informed teacher-student design, and attention to data availability and optimization dynamics — KD yields large practical benefits for deep learning and NLP systems while avoiding common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: The Practical Centrality of Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, versatile technique for shrinking large neural models while preserving much of their predictive power. Across NLP and broader deep learning applications, distillation enables faster inference, reduced memory footprint, and easier deployment in latency- and resource-constrained settings. When combined with teacher ensembles, online or self-distillation, task-adaptive search, and careful handling of soft labels and data augmentation, distillation can deliver near-teacher accuracy while addressing scalability, robustness, and domain transfer concerns. I argue that knowledge distillation should be a first-line approach for model compression in modern NLP pipelines, supplemented by principled choices about teachers, data, and optimization to realize its full benefits.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression techniques have become central to deploying deep models under computation, memory, latency, and privacy constraints. Over the past decade researchers have developed a spectrum of KD methods — teacher→student transfer, feature-level and adversarial distillation, data-free (zero-shot) distillation, online/multi-teacher schemes, and combinations of KD with pruning and architecture search — and applied them across domains including vision, multimodal models, graph and medical data, and NLP. Empirical results repeatedly show that appropriately designed distillation can produce much smaller, faster, or more private models with modest loss (or sometimes gain) in accuracy, while remaining sensitive to dataset availability, domain shift, and adversarial robustness. Current best practices emphasize matching representations beyond logits, designing student-friendly supervision, and combining KD with structural compression; remaining challenges include KD under data heterogeneity or privacy constraints, transferring robustness, and automating student architectures for diverse tasks.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster ones while preserving performance, enabling deployment under resource, latency, privacy, and domain-specific constraints. Across modalities and tasks, KD can be combined with architectural search, feature-level objectives, teacher optimization, and data-free methods to meet diverse production requirements. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a primary instrument in model-compression toolkits for modern deep learning and NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Theory, and Practical Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach to compress large deep models and transfer knowledge to smaller, faster, or more interpretable models. Across vision and language applications, KD encompasses teacher-student paradigms that use teacher soft targets, intermediate representations, or auxiliary objectives; extensions include multi-teacher setups, data-free distillation, meta-learned teachers, and device-aware distillation for heterogeneous deployments. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of the teacher performance while enabling orders-of-magnitude reductions in parameters and inference cost; theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when and why distillation helps and how dataset complexity, teacher quality, and student capacity interact to determine outcomes. Practical strategies combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware techniques to meet deployment constraints while retaining generalization.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans algorithmic advances in teacher–student objectives, architecture-aware compression, data- and privacy-constrained distillation, and theoretical analyses that clarify when and why distillation helps. Practical work shows gains from combining KD with data augmentation, many-to-many layer mappings, and architecture search, while complementary efforts address data-free and privacy-preserving distillation. Remaining challenges include imperfect teachers, data heterogeneity, and adapting compression to task-specific constraints.

When these components are designed together, distilled models can approach teacher-level performance and enable real-world NLP systems at lower latency and cost.'}, {'author': 'Abbott', 'year': 2022, 'title': 'Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation', 'abstract': 'Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.'}, {'author': 'Rice', 'year': 2017, 'title': 'Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practice', 'abstract': "Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller ones by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations from a teacher to a student. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.'}, {'author': 'Rogers', 'year': 2025, 'title': 'Beyond Soft Labels: A Practical Case for Richer Knowledge Distillation in NLP and Deep Learning', 'abstract': 'Knowledge distillation is a necessary and practical tool for compressing large models and enabling deployment in resource-constrained settings, but its value depends critically on what is distilled and how. Soft-label matching transfers useful "dark knowledge" from ensembles, yet by itself often fails to capture internal structure, handle domain or data heterogeneity, or operate when original data are unavailable. Combining soft labels with internal- and feature-level guidance, architecture- and task-aware compression, and data- or privacy-aware generation strategies yields more robust, compact models that retain teacher performance across NLP and broader deep learning tasks.'}, {'author': 'Graham', 'year': 2018, 'title': 'Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning', 'abstract': 'A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The source code is available at our project page.'}, {'author': 'Gonzalez', 'year': 2018, 'title': 'Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Trade-offs', 'abstract': 'Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable smaller or faster models to retain much of the performance of larger teachers by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or task-specific inductive biases. Important trade-offs involve what form of knowledge is transferred (logits, activations, relations), access to training data, robustness to domain heterogeneity, and how to balance capacity, efficiency, and generalization in student models.'}, {'author': 'Rodriguez', 'year': 2021, 'title': 'Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework', 'abstract': 'Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF'}, {'author': 'Martin', 'year': 2024, 'title': 'Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Multi-purpose Strategy for Model Compression and Robust Deployment', 'abstract': 'Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving or even improving task performance.
